given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans are lent on 03-02, so they are due 03-16. Today is then set to 03-17.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database starts empty and the job runs once, so no reminder exists for today.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must equal exactly the two entries, each with its own memberId, loanId and dueOn.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: Each row in the reminders table must have `sent_on` 2026-03-17, and there must be exactly two rows.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so the second run meets a loan that was reminded earlier the same day.
loan2 is overdue and then returned before the job runs.
The third loan is lent on 03-03, so it is due on 03-17, which is today. That sits on the boundary.

then.why: `sent` must contain only loan1, once, so a resend on the second run, a returned loan or a not-yet-overdue loan would each fail it.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with a reason.
B5 proves a failed connection becomes a refused result. The service test only uses a refusal reason.
The job runs with an overdue loan to remind.

then.why: The reminders table must contain only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: The log must contain an exact entry with level warn, the event name, loanId and the refusal reason.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 is sent even though loan1 was refused. loan1 was lent first, so it is likely handled first.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are handled, and one of them is refused.

then.why: The last log entry must have level info and the event `reminders.finished`.
`sent: 2` is asserted for two accepted loans.
A refusal is set up, but `expect.objectContaining({ sent: 2 })` never checks `failed`, so removing or miscounting it would still pass.

given.why: A reminder with memberId, loanId and dueOn is passed straight to the client.

then.why: The captured request's method must be POST and its path /notifications on the notifications host.

then.part: with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The content type and the whole body are compared with `toEqual`.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives kind refused with a reason containing "400".

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives kind refused with a reason containing "unreachable".
